# ---- codex-cli model.patch ----
diff --git a/compile.sh b/compile.sh
index 5fc76ac..f653472 100644
--- a/compile.sh
+++ b/compile.sh
@@ -1,3 +1,14 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env sh
 set -eu
-[ -f executable ]
+
+rm -f executable executable.exe executable.cmd executable.bat executable.js executable.py executable.jar
+
+case "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || printf unknown)" in
+  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
+    printf '%s\r\n' '@echo off' 'python "%~dp0eza_port.py" %*' > executable.cmd
+    ;;
+  *)
+    cp eza_port.py executable
+    chmod +x executable
+    ;;
+esac

use super::file_name::QuoteStyle;
use nu_ansi_term::{AnsiString as ANSIString, Style};
use percent_encoding::{utf8_percent_encode, AsciiSet, CONTROLS};

pub fn escape(
    string: String,
    bits: &mut Vec<ANSIString<'_>>,
    good: Style,
    bad: Style,
    quote_style: QuoteStyle,
) {
    let bits_starting_length = bits.len();
    let needs_quotes = string.contains(' ') || string.contains('\'');
    let quote_bit = good.paint(if string.contains('\'') { "\"" } else { "\'" });

    if string
        .chars()
        .all(|c| c >= 0x20 as char && c != 0x7f as char)
    {
        bits.push(good.paint(string));
    } else {
        for c in string.chars() {
            // The `escape_default` method on `char` is *almost* what we want here, but
            // it still escapes non-ASCII UTF-8 characters, which are still printable.

            // TODO: This allocates way too much,
            // hence the `all` check above.
            if c >= 0x20 as char && c != 0x7f as char {
                bits.push(good.paint(c.to_string()));
            } else {
                bits.push(bad.paint(c.escape_default().to_string()));
            }
        }
    }

    if quote_style != QuoteStyle::NoQuotes && needs_quotes {
        bits.insert(bits_starting_length, quote_bit.clone());
        bits.push(quote_bit);
    }
}

const HYPERLINK_ESCAPE_CHARS: &AsciiSet = &CONTROLS.add(b' ');
const HYPERLINK_OPENING_START: &str = "\x1B]8;;";
const HYPERLINK_OPENING_END: &str = "\x1B\x5C";
// Combination of both above tags
pub const HYPERLINK_CLOSING: &str = "\x1B]8;;\x1B\x5C";

pub fn get_hyperlink_start_tag(abs_path: &str) -> String {
    let abs_path = utf8_percent_encode(abs_path, HYPERLINK_ESCAPE_CHARS).to_string();

    // On Windows, `std::fs::canonicalize` adds the Win32 File prefix, which we need to remove
    #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
    let abs_path = abs_path.strip_prefix("\\\\?\\").unwrap_or(&abs_path);

    format!("{HYPERLINK_OPENING_START}file://{abs_path}{HYPERLINK_OPENING_END}")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod test {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hyperlink_start_tag_escape_spaces() {
        assert_eq!(
            get_hyperlink_start_tag("/folder name/file name").to_string(),
            format!(
                "{HYPERLINK_OPENING_START}file:///folder%20name/file%20name{HYPERLINK_OPENING_END}"
            ),
        );
    }
}

+                        i += 1
+                    else:
+                        raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    break
+                else:
+                    if j < len(body):
+                        value = body[j:]
+                        if spec.choices and value not in spec.choices:
+                            raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
+                        j = len(body)
+                    elif i < len(argv) and spec.choices and argv[i] in spec.choices:
+                        value = argv[i]
+                        i += 1
+                    else:
+                        value = spec.default
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    break
+            continue
+        parsed.paths.append(token)
+    return parsed
+
+
+def _bad_argument(spec_name: str, value: str) -> OptionError:
+    spec = BY_LONG[spec_name]
+    suffix = f" ({_choices_text(spec.choices)})" if spec.takes == "necessary" and spec.choices else ""
+    escaped = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
+    return OptionError(f'Option {spec.label()} has no "{escaped}" setting{suffix}')
+
+
+def _parse_usize(value: str, source: str) -> int:
+    if not value or not value.isascii() or not value.isdigit():
+        raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: invalid digit found in string')
+    result = int(value, 10)
+    if result > (1 << 64) - 1:
+        raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: number too large to fit in target type')
+    return result
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Options:
+    mode: str = "lines"  # lines, grid, details, grid-details
+    tree: bool = False
+    recurse: bool = False
+    as_file: bool = False
+    level: Optional[int] = None
+    dot_mode: int = 0
+    sort: str = "name"
+    reverse: bool = False
+    dirs_first: bool = False
+    dirs_last: bool = False
+    only_dirs: bool = False
+    only_files: bool = False
+    no_symlinks: bool = False
+    show_symlinks: bool = False
+    ignore_patterns: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    across: bool = False
+    width: Optional[int] = None
+    quote: bool = True
+    classify: str = "never"
+    absolute: str = "off"
+    deref: bool = False
+    follow_links: bool = False
+    hyperlink: bool = False
+    header: bool = False
+    permissions: bool = True
+    filesize: bool = True
+    time_fields: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["modified"])
+    time_style: str = "default"
+    size_style: str = "decimal"
+    file_flags: bool = False
+    stdin: bool = False
+
+
+def deduce_options(parsed: Parsed) -> Options:
+    opts = Options()
+
+    width_value = parsed.last_value("width")
+    if width_value is not None:
+        width = _parse_usize(width_value, BY_LONG["width"].label())
+        opts.width = width if width >= 1 else None
+    elif "COLUMNS" in os.environ:
+        value = os.environ["COLUMNS"]
+        if not value.isdigit():
+            raise OptionError(
+                f'Value "{value}" not valid for environment variable COLUMNS: invalid digit found in string'
+            )
+        opts.width = int(value)
+
+    is_tty = opts.width is not None or sys.stdout.isatty()
+    view_flag = parsed.last_flag("long", "oneline", "grid", "tree")
+    if view_flag is None:
+        opts.mode = "grid" if is_tty else "lines"
+    elif view_flag == "long" or (view_flag == "tree" and parsed.has("long")) or (
+        view_flag == "grid" and parsed.has("long")
+    ):
+        grid_tree_flag = parsed.last_flag("grid", "tree")
+        opts.mode = "grid-details" if grid_tree_flag == "grid" else "details"
+    elif view_flag == "tree":
+        opts.mode = "details"
+    elif view_flag == "oneline":
+        opts.mode = "lines"
+    else:
+        opts.mode = "grid"
+
+    requested_tree = parsed.has("tree")
+    opts.tree = requested_tree and opts.mode == "details"
+    opts.recurse = opts.tree or parsed.has("recurse")
+    opts.as_file = (parsed.has("treat-dirs-as-files") or parsed.has("list-dirs")) and not opts.recurse
+
+    level_value = parsed.last_value("level")
+    if level_value is not None:
+        opts.level = _parse_usize(level_value, BY_LONG["level"].label())
+
+    all_count = parsed.count("all")
+    if all_count >= 2 and requested_tree:
+        raise OptionError("Option --tree is useless given --all --all")
+    opts.dot_mode = 2 if all_count >= 2 else (1 if all_count or parsed.has("almost-all") else 0)
+
+    sort_value = parsed.last_value("sort")
+    aliases = {
+        "name": "name", "filename": "name", "Name": "Name", "Filename": "Name",
+        ".name": ".name", ".filename": ".name", ".Name": ".Name", ".Filename": ".Name",
+        "size": "size", "filesize": "size", "ext": "extension", "extension": "extension",
+        "Ext": "Extension", "Extension": "Extension", "date": "modified", "time": "modified",
+        "mod": "modified", "modified": "modified", "new": "modified", "newest": "modified",
+        "age": "age", "old": "age", "oldest": "age", "ch": "changed", "changed": "changed",
+        "acc": "accessed", "accessed": "accessed", "cr": "created", "created": "created",
+        "type": "type", "none": "none",
+    }
+    if sort_value is not None:
+        if sort_value not in aliases:
+            raise _bad_argument("sort", sort_value)
+        opts.sort = aliases[sort_value]
+
+    opts.reverse = parsed.has("reverse")
+    opts.dirs_first = parsed.has("group-directories-first")
+    opts.dirs_last = parsed.has("group-directories-last")
+    opts.only_dirs = parsed.has("only-dirs")
+    opts.only_files = parsed.has("only-files")
+    opts.no_symlinks = parsed.has("no-symlinks")
+    opts.show_symlinks = parsed.has("show-symlinks")
+    ignore = parsed.last_value("ignore-glob")
+    opts.ignore_patterns = [] if ignore is None else ignore.split("|")
+    opts.across = parsed.has("across")
+    opts.quote = not parsed.has("no-quotes")
+    opts.deref = parsed.has("dereference")
+    opts.follow_links = parsed.has("follow-symlinks")
+    opts.hyperlink = parsed.has("hyperlink")
+
+    classify = parsed.last_value("classify")
+    if classify is not None:
+        if classify not in ("always", "auto", "automatic", "never"):
+            raise _bad_argument("classify", classify)
+        opts.classify = "always" if classify == "always" else ("always" if classify in ("auto", "automatic") and sys.stdout.isatty() else "never")
+
+    absolute = parsed.last_value("absolute")
+    if absolute is not None:
+        mapping = {"on": "on", "yes": "on", "follow": "follow", "off": "off", "no": "off"}
+        if absolute not in mapping:
+            raise _bad_argument("absolute", absolute)
+        opts.absolute = mapping[absolute]
+
+    opts.header = parsed.has("header")
+    opts.permissions = not parsed.has("no-permissions")
+    opts.filesize = not parsed.has("no-filesize")
+    opts.file_flags = parsed.has("flags")
+    if parsed.has("bytes") and (not parsed.has("binary") or parsed.last_flag("binary", "bytes") == "bytes"):
+        opts.size_style = "bytes"
+    elif parsed.has("binary"):
+        opts.size_style = "binary"
+
+    time_word = parsed.last_value("time")
+    selected = []
+    if parsed.has("no-time"):
+        selected = []
+    elif time_word is not None:
+        tmapping = {"mod": "modified", "modified": "modified", "ch": "changed", "changed": "changed", "acc": "accessed", "accessed": "accessed", "cr": "created", "created": "created"}
+        if time_word not in tmapping:
+            raise _bad_argument("time", time_word)
+        selected = [tmapping[time_word]]
+    else:
+        for flag_name in ("modified", "changed", "created", "accessed"):
+            if parsed.has(flag_name):
+                selected.append(flag_name)
+        if not selected:
+            selected = ["modified"]
+    opts.time_fields = selected
+
+    time_style = parsed.last_value("time-style")
+    if time_style is None:
+        time_style = os.environ.get("TIME_STYLE") or "default"
+    if time_style not in ("default", "relative", "iso", "long-iso", "full-iso") and not time_style.startswith("+"):
+        raise _bad_argument("time-style", time_style)
+    opts.time_style = time_style
+    opts.stdin = parsed.has("stdin") or not sys.stdin.isatty()
+    return opts
+
+
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY = 0x00000001
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN = 0x00000002
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM = 0x00000004
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY = 0x00000010
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE = 0x00000020
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT = 0x00000400
+
+
+def _path_name(path: str) -> str:
+    normalized = ntpath.normpath(path)
+    name = ntpath.basename(normalized)
+    if name:
+        return name
+    if path in (".", ".."):
+        return path
+    drive, tail = ntpath.splitdrive(normalized)
+    return tail or drive or path
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FileInfo:
+    path: str
+    name: str
+    parented: bool = False
+    is_all_all: bool = False
+    _lstat: Optional[os.stat_result] = None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def argument(cls, path: str) -> "FileInfo":
+        return cls(path=path, name=_path_name(path))
+
+    @classmethod
+    def child(cls, directory: str, name: str, st: Optional[os.stat_result] = None) -> "FileInfo":
+        return cls(path=ntpath.join(directory, name), name=name, parented=True, _lstat=st)
+
+    def lstat(self) -> os.stat_result:
+        if self._lstat is None:
+            self._lstat = os.lstat(self.path)
+        return self._lstat
+
+    def followed_stat(self) -> os.stat_result:
+        return os.stat(self.path)
+
+    def attrs(self) -> int:
+        st = self.lstat()
+        attrs = getattr(st, "st_file_attributes", 0)
+        if attrs:
+            return int(attrs)
+        result = 0
+        if _stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY
+        elif _stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE
+        if not os.access(self.path, os.W_OK):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY
+        if self.is_link():
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT
+        return result
+
+    def is_link(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISLNK(self.lstat().st_mode) or bool(self.attrs() & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT and os.path.islink(self.path))
+
+    def is_dir(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISDIR(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()
+
+    def is_file(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISREG(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()
+
+    def points_to_dir(self) -> bool:
+        if self.is_dir():
+            return True
+        if self.is_link():
+            try:
+                return os.path.isdir(self.path)
+            except OSError:
+                return False
+        return False
+
+    def length(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.lstat().st_size)
+
+    def extension(self) -> Optional[str]:
+        pos = self.name.rfind(".")
+        return None if pos < 0 else self.name[pos + 1 :].lower()
+
+    def time_ns(self, which: str, deref: bool = False) -> Optional[int]:
+        try:
+            st = self.followed_stat() if deref and self.is_link() else self.lstat()
+        except OSError:
+            return None
+        if which in ("modified", "changed"):
+            return int(st.st_mtime_ns)
+        if which == "accessed":
+            return int(st.st_atime_ns)
+        birth_ns = getattr(st, "st_birthtime_ns", None)
+        return int(birth_ns if birth_ns is not None else st.st_ctime_ns)
+
+
+_NATURAL_PARTS = re.compile(r"(\d+)")
+
+
+def _natural_chunks(value: str, insensitive: bool) -> list[tuple[int, object, object]]:
+    if insensitive:
+        value = value.lower()
+    chunks: list[tuple[int, object, object]] = []
+    for part in _NATURAL_PARTS.split(value):
+        if not part:
+            continue
+        if part.isdigit():
+            significant = part.lstrip("0") or "0"
+            chunks.append((0, len(significant), significant))
+        else:
+            chunks.append((1, part, ""))
+    return chunks
+
+
+def _compare_values(a, b) -> int:
+    return (a > b) - (a < b)
+
+
+def _natural_compare(a: str, b: str, insensitive: bool) -> int:
+    ac = _natural_chunks(a, insensitive)
+    bc = _natural_chunks(b, insensitive)
+    for left, right in zip(ac, bc):
+        result = _compare_values(left, right)
+        if result:
+            return result
+    return _compare_values(len(ac), len(bc))
+
+
+def compare_files(a: FileInfo, b: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> int:
+    field_name = opts.sort
+    if field_name == "none":
+        return 0
+    if field_name in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name"):
+        an = a.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and a.name.startswith(".") else a.name
+        bn = b.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and b.name.startswith(".") else b.name
+        return _natural_compare(an, bn, field_name in ("name", ".name"))
+    if field_name in ("extension", "Extension"):
+        ae, be = a.extension(), b.extension()
+        if ae is None or be is None:
+            result = _compare_values(ae is not None, be is not None)
+        else:
+            result = _compare_values(ae, be)
+        if result:
+            return result
+        return _natural_compare(a.name, b.name, field_name == "extension")
+    if field_name == "size":
+        return _compare_values(a.length(), b.length())
+    if field_name in ("modified", "changed", "accessed", "created", "age"):
+        left = a.time_ns(field_name if field_name != "age" else "modified", opts.deref)
+        right = b.time_ns(field_name if field_name != "age" else "modified", opts.deref)
+        lk = (-1 if left is None else left)
+        rk = (-1 if right is None else right)
+        result = _compare_values(lk, rk)
+        return -result if field_name == "age" else result
+    if field_name == "type":
+        def rank(f: FileInfo) -> int:
+            if f.is_dir(): return 0
+            if f.is_file(): return 1
+            return 7
+        result = _compare_values(rank(a), rank(b))
+        return result or _natural_compare(a.name, b.name, False)
+    return 0
+
+
+def sort_files(files: list[FileInfo], opts: Options) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    files.sort(key=functools.cmp_to_key(lambda a, b: compare_files(a, b, opts)))
+    if opts.reverse:
+        files.reverse()
+    if opts.dirs_first:
+        files.sort(key=lambda f: not f.points_to_dir())
+    elif opts.dirs_last:
+        files.sort(key=lambda f: f.points_to_dir())
+    return files
+
+
+def _ignored(name: str, patterns: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
+    return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern) for pattern in patterns)
+
+
+def filter_children(files: list[FileInfo], opts: Options, is_recurse: bool) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    result = [f for f in files if not _ignored(f.name, opts.ignore_patterns)]
+    filtered: list[FileInfo] = []
+    for f in result:
+        keep = True
+        if opts.only_dirs and not opts.only_files:
+            keep = f.is_dir() or (opts.show_symlinks and f.points_to_dir())
+        elif opts.only_files and not opts.only_dirs:
+            if is_recurse:
+                keep = True
+            elif opts.show_symlinks:
+                keep = f.is_file() or (f.is_link() and not f.points_to_dir())
+            else:
+                keep = f.is_file()
+        elif opts.no_symlinks and not opts.show_symlinks:
+            keep = not f.is_link()
+        if keep:
+            filtered.append(f)
+    return filtered
+
+
+def read_children(directory: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    children: list[FileInfo] = []
+    if opts.dot_mode == 2:
+        current = FileInfo(directory.path, ".", True, True)
+        parent = FileInfo(ntpath.join(directory.path, ".."), "..", True, True)
+        children.extend((current, parent))
+    with os.scandir(directory.path) as entries:
+        for entry in entries:
+            name = entry.name
+            try:
+                st = entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
+            except OSError:
+                st = None
+            child = FileInfo.child(directory.path, name, st)
+            if opts.dot_mode == 0:
+                if name.startswith(".") or name.startswith("_"):
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    if child.attrs() & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN:
+                        continue
+                except OSError:
+                    pass
+            children.append(child)
+    return children
+
+
+def _escape_control(text: str) -> str:
+    pieces = []
+    mapping = {"\t": "\\t", "\r": "\\r", "\n": "\\n", "\0": "\\0", "\\": "\\\\", "'": "\\'", '"': '\\"'}
+    for char in text:
+        code = ord(char)
+        if code >= 0x20 and code != 0x7F:
+            pieces.append(char)
+        elif char in mapping:
+            pieces.append(mapping[char])
+        else:
+            pieces.append(f"\\u{{{code:x}}}")
+    return "".join(pieces)
+
+
+def escape_name(text: str, quote: bool) -> str:
+    escaped = _escape_control(text)
+    needs_quotes = " " in text or "'" in text
+    if quote and needs_quotes:
+        mark = '"' if "'" in text else "'"
+        return mark + escaped + mark
+    return escaped
+
+
+def _normal_display_path(path: str) -> str:
+    return ntpath.normpath(path)
+
+
+def display_base_name(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> str:
+    if opts.absolute == "on":
+        raw = ntpath.abspath(file.path)
+        return escape_name(_normal_display_path(raw), opts.quote)
+    if opts.absolute == "follow":
+        try:
+            raw = os.path.realpath(file.path)
+        except OSError:
+            raw = ntpath.abspath(file.path)
+        return escape_name(_normal_display_path(raw), opts.quote)
+    prefix = ""
+    if not file.parented:
+        parent = ntpath.dirname(_normal_display_path(file.path))
+        if parent:
+            prefix = escape_name(parent, opts.quote) + "\\"
+    return prefix + escape_name(file.name, opts.quote)
+
+
+def _classify(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> str:
+    if opts.classify != "always":
+        return ""
+    if file.is_dir():
+        return "/"
+    if file.is_link():
+        return "@"
+    return ""
+
+
+def _link_target_text(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> Optional[str]:
+    if not file.is_link() or opts.deref:
+        return None
+    try:
+        target_path = os.readlink(file.path)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    if target_path.startswith("\\\\?\\"):
+        target_path = target_path[4:]
+    target_exists = os.path.exists(file.path)
+    if not target_exists:
+        return escape_name(target_path, opts.quote)
+    parent = ntpath.dirname(_normal_display_path(target_path))
+    name = _path_name(target_path)
+    shown = (escape_name(parent, opts.quote) + "\\" if parent else "") + escape_name(name, opts.quote)
+    try:
+        target_info = FileInfo(target_path if ntpath.isabs(target_path) else ntpath.join(ntpath.dirname(file.path), target_path), name)
+        shown += _classify(target_info, opts)
+    except OSError:
+        pass
+    return shown
+
+
+def display_name(file: FileInfo, opts: Options, show_link: bool = True) -> str:
+    result = display_base_name(file, opts)
+    target = _link_target_text(file, opts) if show_link else None
+    if target is not None:
+        result += " -> " + target
+    else:
+        result += _classify(file, opts)
+    if opts.hyperlink:
+        try:
+            absolute = os.path.realpath(file.path)
+            uri_path = absolute.replace(" ", "%20")
+            result = f"\x1b]8;;file://{uri_path}\x1b\\{result}\x1b]8;;\x1b\\"
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+    return result
+
+
+def display_width(text: str) -> int:
+    width = 0
+    in_escape = False
+    for char in text:
+        if char == "\x1b":
+            in_escape = True
+            continue
+        if in_escape:
+            if char == "\\":
+                in_escape = False
+            continue
+        if unicodedata.combining(char):
+            continue
+        width += 2 if unicodedata.east_asian_width(char) in ("W", "F") else 1
+    return width
+
+
+def permissions_text(file: FileInfo) -> str:
+    attrs = file.attrs()
+    kind = "l" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT else ("d" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY else "-")
+    return kind + ("a" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE else "-") + ("r" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY else "-") + ("h" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN else "-") + ("s" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM else "-")
+
+
+def _round_rust(value: float) -> int:
+    return int(math.floor(value + 0.5))
+
+
+def size_text(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> str:
+    if file.is_dir():
+        return "-"
+    size = file.length()
+    if opts.size_style == "bytes":
+        return f"{size:,}"
+    if opts.size_style == "binary":
+        base, symbols = 1024.0, ("", "Ki", "Mi", "Gi", "Ti", "Pi", "Ei")
+    else:
+        base, symbols = 1000.0, ("", "k", "M", "G", "T", "P", "E")
+    if size < base:
+        return f"{size:,}"
+    power = min(int(math.log(size, base)), len(symbols) - 1)
+    number = size / (base ** power)
+    shown = f"{number:.1f}" if number < 10 else f"{_round_rust(number):,}"
+    return shown + symbols[power]
+
+
+FLAG_DEFS = (
+    (0x1, "readonly", "R"), (0x2, "hidden", "H"), (0x4, "system", "S"),
+    (0x20, "archive", "A"), (0x100, "temporary", "T"), (0x800, "compressed", "C"),
+    (0x1000, "offline", "O"), (0x2000, "not indexed", "I"), (0x4000, "encrypted", "E"),
+    (0x20000, "no scrub", "X"), (0x100000, "unpinned", "U"), (0x80000, "pinned", "P"),
+    (0x400000, "recall on data access", "M"),
+)
+
+
+def flags_text(file: FileInfo) -> str:
+    attrs = file.attrs()
+    short = os.environ.get("EZA_WINDOWS_ATTRIBUTES", "").lower() == "short"
+    values = [abbr if short else name for bit, name, abbr in FLAG_DEFS if attrs & bit]
+    return "".join(values) if short and values else ("-".join(values) if values else "-")
+
+
+def _current_offset() -> _datetime.timedelta:
+    return _datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().utcoffset() or _datetime.timedelta(0)
+

+def _datetime_for_ns(ns: int) -> _datetime.datetime:

+        return None
+
+    def last_flag(self, *names: str) -> Optional[str]:
+        wanted = set(names)
+        for occurrence in reversed(self.occurrences):
+            if occurrence.spec.long in wanted and occurrence.value is None:
+                return occurrence.spec.long
+        return None
+
+
+def _choices_text(choices: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
+    return "choices: " + ", ".join(choices)
+
+
+def _flag_needs_value(shown: str, choices: Optional[tuple[str, ...]]) -> OptionError:
+    suffix = f" ({_choices_text(choices)})" if choices else ""
+    return OptionError(f"Flag {shown} needs a value{suffix}")
+
+
+def parse_argv(argv: list[str]) -> Parsed:
+    parsed = Parsed()
+    parsing = True
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(argv):
+        token = argv[i]
+        i += 1
+        if not parsing:
+            parsed.paths.append(token)
+            continue
+        if token == "--":
+            parsing = False
+            continue
+        if token.startswith("--"):
+            body = token[2:]
+            before = body
+            after = None
+            if "=" in body:
+                b, a = body.split("=", 1)
+                if b and a:
+                    before, after = b, a
+            spec = BY_LONG.get(before)
+            if spec is None:
+                raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument --{before}")
+            shown = f"--{spec.long}"
+            if after is not None:
+                if spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                    raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, after))
+            elif spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, None))
+            elif spec.takes == "necessary":
+                if i >= len(argv):
+                    raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, argv[i]))
+                i += 1
+            else:
+                if i < len(argv) and spec.choices and argv[i] in spec.choices:
+                    value = argv[i]
+                    i += 1
+                else:
+                    value = spec.default
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+            continue
+        if token.startswith("-") and token != "-":
+            body = token[1:]
+            if "=" in body:
+                before, after = body.split("=", 1)
+                if before and after:
+                    for char in before[:-1]:
+                        spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                        if spec is None:
+                            raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                        shown = f"-{char}"
+                        if spec.takes == "necessary":
+                            raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
+                        value = spec.default if spec.takes == "optional" else None
+                        parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    char = before[-1]
+                    spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                    if spec is None:
+                        raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                    shown = f"-{char}"
+                    if spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                        raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, after))
+                    continue
+            j = 0
+            while j < len(body):
+                char = body[j]
+                spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                if spec is None:
+                    raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                shown = f"-{char}"
+                j += 1
+                if spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, None))
+                elif spec.takes == "necessary":
+                    if j < len(body):
+                        value = body[j:]
+                        j = len(body)
+                    elif i < len(argv):
+                        value = argv[i]
+                        i += 1
+                    else:
+                        raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    break
+                else:
+                    if j < len(body):
+                        value = body[j:]
+                        if spec.choices and value not in spec.choices:
+                            raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
+                        j = len(body)
+                    elif i < len(argv) and spec.choices and argv[i] in spec.choices:
+                        value = argv[i]
+                        i += 1
+                    else:
+                        value = spec.default
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    break
+            continue
+        parsed.paths.append(token)
+    return parsed
+
+
+def _bad_argument(spec_name: str, value: str) -> OptionError:
+    spec = BY_LONG[spec_name]
+    suffix = f" ({_choices_text(spec.choices)})" if spec.takes == "necessary" and spec.choices else ""
+    escaped = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
+    return OptionError(f'Option {spec.label()} has no "{escaped}" setting{suffix}')
+
+
+def _parse_usize(value: str, source: str) -> int:
+    if not value or not value.isascii() or not value.isdigit():
+        raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: invalid digit found in string')
+    result = int(value, 10)
+    if result > (1 << 64) - 1:
+        raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: number too large to fit in target type')
+    return result
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Options:
+    mode: str = "lines"  # lines, grid, details, grid-details
+    tree: bool = False
+    recurse: bool = False
+    as_file: bool = False
+    level: Optional[int] = None
+    dot_mode: int = 0
+    sort: str = "name"
+    reverse: bool = False
+    dirs_first: bool = False
+    dirs_last: bool = False
+    only_dirs: bool = False
+    only_files: bool = False
+    no_symlinks: bool = False
+    show_symlinks: bool = False
+    ignore_patterns: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    across: bool = False
+    width: Optional[int] = None
+    quote: bool = True
+    classify: str = "never"
+    absolute: str = "off"
+    deref: bool = False
+    follow_links: bool = False
+    hyperlink: bool = False
+    header: bool = False
+    permissions: bool = True
+    filesize: bool = True
+    time_fields: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["modified"])
+    time_style: str = "default"
+    size_style: str = "decimal"
+    file_flags: bool = False
+    stdin: bool = False
+
+
+def deduce_options(parsed: Parsed) -> Options:
+    opts = Options()
+
+    width_value = parsed.last_value("width")
+    if width_value is not None:
+        width = _parse_usize(width_value, BY_LONG["width"].label())
+        opts.width = width if width >= 1 else None
+    elif "COLUMNS" in os.environ:
+        value = os.environ["COLUMNS"]
+        if not value.isdigit():
+            raise OptionError(
+                f'Value "{value}" not valid for environment variable COLUMNS: invalid digit found in string'
+            )
+        opts.width = int(value)
+
+    is_tty = opts.width is not None or sys.stdout.isatty()
+    view_flag = parsed.last_flag("long", "oneline", "grid", "tree")
+    if view_flag is None:
+        opts.mode = "grid" if is_tty else "lines"
+    elif view_flag == "long" or (view_flag == "tree" and parsed.has("long")) or (
+        view_flag == "grid" and parsed.has("long")
+    ):
+        grid_tree_flag = parsed.last_flag("grid", "tree")
+        opts.mode = "grid-details" if grid_tree_flag == "grid" else "details"
+    elif view_flag == "tree":
+        opts.mode = "details"
+    elif view_flag == "oneline":
+        opts.mode = "lines"
+    else:
+        opts.mode = "grid"
+
+    requested_tree = parsed.has("tree")
+    opts.tree = requested_tree and opts.mode == "details"
+    opts.recurse = opts.tree or parsed.has("recurse")
+    opts.as_file = (parsed.has("treat-dirs-as-files") or parsed.has("list-dirs")) and not opts.recurse
+
+    level_value = parsed.last_value("level")
+    if level_value is not None:
+        opts.level = _parse_usize(level_value, BY_LONG["level"].label())
+
+    all_count = parsed.count("all")
+    if all_count >= 2 and requested_tree:
+        raise OptionError("Option --tree is useless given --all --all")
+    opts.dot_mode = 2 if all_count >= 2 else (1 if all_count or parsed.has("almost-all") else 0)
+
+    sort_value = parsed.last_value("sort")
+    aliases = {
+        "name": "name", "filename": "name", "Name": "Name", "Filename": "Name",
+        ".name": ".name", ".filename": ".name", ".Name": ".Name", ".Filename": ".Name",
+        "size": "size", "filesize": "size", "ext": "extension", "extension": "extension",
+        "Ext": "Extension", "Extension": "Extension", "date": "modified", "time": "modified",
+        "mod": "modified", "modified": "modified", "new": "modified", "newest": "modified",
+        "age": "age", "old": "age", "oldest": "age", "ch": "changed", "changed": "changed",
+        "acc": "accessed", "accessed": "accessed", "cr": "created", "created": "created",
+        "type": "type", "none": "none",
+    }
+    if sort_value is not None:
+        if sort_value not in aliases:
+            raise _bad_argument("sort", sort_value)
+        opts.sort = aliases[sort_value]
+
+    opts.reverse = parsed.has("reverse")
+    opts.dirs_first = parsed.has("group-directories-first")
+    opts.dirs_last = parsed.has("group-directories-last")
+    opts.only_dirs = parsed.has("only-dirs")
+    opts.only_files = parsed.has("only-files")
+    opts.no_symlinks = parsed.has("no-symlinks")
+    opts.show_symlinks = parsed.has("show-symlinks")
+    ignore = parsed.last_value("ignore-glob")
+    opts.ignore_patterns = [] if ignore is None else ignore.split("|")
+    opts.across = parsed.has("across")
+    opts.quote = not parsed.has("no-quotes")
+    opts.deref = parsed.has("dereference")
+    opts.follow_links = parsed.has("follow-symlinks")
+    opts.hyperlink = parsed.has("hyperlink")
+
+    classify = parsed.last_value("classify")
+    if classify is not None:
+        if classify not in ("always", "auto", "automatic", "never"):
+            raise _bad_argument("classify", classify)
+        opts.classify = "always" if classify == "always" else ("always" if classify in ("auto", "automatic") and sys.stdout.isatty() else "never")
+
+    absolute = parsed.last_value("absolute")
+    if absolute is not None:
+        mapping = {"on": "on", "yes": "on", "follow": "follow", "off": "off", "no": "off"}
+        if absolute not in mapping:
+            raise _bad_argument("absolute", absolute)
+        opts.absolute = mapping[absolute]
+
+    opts.header = parsed.has("header")
+    opts.permissions = not parsed.has("no-permissions")
+    opts.filesize = not parsed.has("no-filesize")
+    opts.file_flags = parsed.has("flags")
+    if parsed.has("bytes") and (not parsed.has("binary") or parsed.last_flag("binary", "bytes") == "bytes"):
+        opts.size_style = "bytes"
+    elif parsed.has("binary"):
+        opts.size_style = "binary"
+
+    time_word = parsed.last_value("time")
+    selected = []
+    if parsed.has("no-time"):
+        selected = []
+    elif time_word is not None:
+        tmapping = {"mod": "modified", "modified": "modified", "ch": "changed", "changed": "changed", "acc": "accessed", "accessed": "accessed", "cr": "created", "created": "created"}
+        if time_word not in tmapping:
+            raise _bad_argument("time", time_word)
+        selected = [tmapping[time_word]]
+    else:
+        for flag_name in ("modified", "changed", "created", "accessed"):
+            if parsed.has(flag_name):
+                selected.append(flag_name)
+        if not selected:
+            selected = ["modified"]
+    opts.time_fields = selected
+
+    time_style = parsed.last_value("time-style")
+    if time_style is None:
+        time_style = os.environ.get("TIME_STYLE") or "default"
+    if time_style not in ("default", "relative", "iso", "long-iso", "full-iso") and not time_style.startswith("+"):
+        raise _bad_argument("time-style", time_style)
+    opts.time_style = time_style
+    opts.stdin = parsed.has("stdin") or not sys.stdin.isatty()
+    return opts
+
+
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY = 0x00000001
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN = 0x00000002
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM = 0x00000004
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY = 0x00000010
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE = 0x00000020
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT = 0x00000400
+
+
+def _path_name(path: str) -> str:
+    normalized = ntpath.normpath(path)
+    name = ntpath.basename(normalized)
+    if name:
+        return name
+    if path in (".", ".."):
+        return path
+    drive, tail = ntpath.splitdrive(normalized)
+    return tail or drive or path
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FileInfo:
+    path: str
+    name: str
+    parented: bool = False
+    is_all_all: bool = False
+    _lstat: Optional[os.stat_result] = None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def argument(cls, path: str) -> "FileInfo":
+        return cls(path=path, name=_path_name(path))
+
+    @classmethod
+    def child(cls, directory: str, name: str, st: Optional[os.stat_result] = None) -> "FileInfo":
+        return cls(path=ntpath.join(directory, name), name=name, parented=True, _lstat=st)
+
+    def lstat(self) -> os.stat_result:
+        if self._lstat is None:
+            self._lstat = os.lstat(self.path)
+        return self._lstat
+
+    def followed_stat(self) -> os.stat_result:
+        return os.stat(self.path)
+
+    def attrs(self) -> int:
+        st = self.lstat()
+        attrs = getattr(st, "st_file_attributes", 0)
+        if attrs:
+            return int(attrs)
+        result = 0
+        if _stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY
+        elif _stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE
+        if not os.access(self.path, os.W_OK):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY
+        if self.is_link():
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT
+        return result
+
+    def is_link(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISLNK(self.lstat().st_mode) or bool(self.attrs() & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT and os.path.islink(self.path))
+
+    def is_dir(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISDIR(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()
+
+    def is_file(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISREG(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()
+
+    def points_to_dir(self) -> bool:
+        if self.is_dir():
+            return True
+        if self.is_link():
+            try:
+                return os.path.isdir(self.path)
+            except OSError:
+                return False
+        return False
+
+    def length(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.lstat().st_size)
+
+    def extension(self) -> Optional[str]:
+        pos = self.name.rfind(".")
+        return None if pos < 0 else self.name[pos + 1 :].lower()
+
+    def time_ns(self, which: str, deref: bool = False) -> Optional[int]:
+        try:
+            st = self.followed_stat() if deref and self.is_link() else self.lstat()
+        except OSError:
+            return None
+        if which in ("modified", "changed"):
+            return int(st.st_mtime_ns)
+        if which == "accessed":
+            return int(st.st_atime_ns)
+        birth_ns = getattr(st, "st_birthtime_ns", None)
+        return int(birth_ns if birth_ns is not None else st.st_ctime_ns)
+
+
+_NATURAL_PARTS = re.compile(r"(\d+)")
+
+
+def _natural_chunks(value: str, insensitive: bool) -> list[tuple[int, object, object]]:
+    if insensitive:
+        value = value.lower()
+    chunks: list[tuple[int, object, object]] = []
+    for part in _NATURAL_PARTS.split(value):
+        if not part:
+            continue
+        if part.isdigit():
+            significant = part.lstrip("0") or "0"
+            chunks.append((0, len(significant), significant))
+        else:
+            chunks.append((1, part, ""))
+    return chunks
+
+
+def _compare_values(a, b) -> int:
+    return (a > b) - (a < b)
+
+
+def _natural_compare(a: str, b: str, insensitive: bool) -> int:
+    ac = _natural_chunks(a, insensitive)
+    bc = _natural_chunks(b, insensitive)
+    for left, right in zip(ac, bc):
+        result = _compare_values(left, right)
+        if result:
+            return result
+    return _compare_values(len(ac), len(bc))
+
+
+def compare_files(a: FileInfo, b: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> int:
+    field_name = opts.sort
+    if field_name == "none":
+        return 0
+    if field_name in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name"):
+        an = a.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and a.name.startswith(".") else a.name
+        bn = b.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and b.name.startswith(".") else b.name
+        return _natural_compare(an, bn, field_name in ("name", ".name"))
+    if field_name in ("extension", "Extension"):
+        ae, be = a.extension(), b.extension()
+        if ae is None or be is None:
+            result = _compare_values(ae is not None, be is not None)
+        else:
+            result = _compare_values(ae, be)
+        if result:
+            return result
+        return _natural_compare(a.name, b.name, field_name == "extension")
+    if field_name == "size":
+        return _compare_values(a.length(), b.length())
+    if field_name in ("modified", "changed", "accessed", "created", "age"):
+        left = a.time_ns(field_name if field_name != "age" else "modified", opts.deref)
+        right = b.time_ns(field_name if field_name != "age" else "modified", opts.deref)
+        lk = (-1 if left is None else left)
+        rk = (-1 if right is None else right)
+        result = _compare_values(lk, rk)
+        return -result if field_name == "age" else result
+    if field_name == "type":
+        def rank(f: FileInfo) -> int:
+            if f.is_dir(): return 0
+            if f.is_file(): return 1
+            return 7
+        result = _compare_values(rank(a), rank(b))
+        return result or _natural_compare(a.name, b.name, False)
+    return 0
+
+
+def sort_files(files: list[FileInfo], opts: Options) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    files.sort(key=functools.cmp_to_key(lambda a, b: compare_files(a, b, opts)))
+    if opts.reverse:
+        files.reverse()
+    if opts.dirs_first:
+        files.sort(key=lambda f: not f.points_to_dir())
+    elif opts.dirs_last:
+        files.sort(key=lambda f: f.points_to_dir())
+    return files
+
+
+def _ignored(name: str, patterns: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
+    return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern) for pattern in patterns)
+
+
+def filter_children(files: list[FileInfo], opts: Options, is_recurse: bool) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    result = [f for f in files if not _ignored(f.name, opts.ignore_patterns)]
+    filtered: list[FileInfo] = []
+    for f in result:
+        keep = True
+        if opts.only_dirs and not opts.only_files:
+            keep = f.is_dir() or (opts.show_symlinks and f.points_to_dir())
+        elif opts.only_files and not opts.only_dirs:
+            if is_recurse:
+                keep = True
+            elif opts.show_symlinks:
+                keep = f.is_file() or (f.is_link() and not f.points_to_dir())
+            else:
+                keep = f.is_file()
+        elif opts.no_symlinks and not opts.show_symlinks:
+            keep = not f.is_link()
+        if keep:
+            filtered.append(f)
+    return filtered
+
+
+def read_children(directory: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    children: list[FileInfo] = []
+    if opts.dot_mode == 2:
+        current = FileInfo(directory.path, ".", True, True)
+        parent = FileInfo(ntpath.join(directory.path, ".."), "..", True, True)
+        children.extend((current, parent))
+    with os.scandir(directory.path) as entries:
+        for entry in entries:
+            name = entry.name
+            try:
+                st = entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
+            except OSError:
+                st = None
+            child = FileInfo.child(directory.path, name, st)
+            if opts.dot_mode == 0:
+                if name.startswith(".") or name.startswith("_"):
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    if child.attrs() & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN:
+                        continue
+                except OSError:
+                    pass
+            children.append(child)
+    return children
+

+def _escape_control(text: str) -> str:
+    pieces = []
+    mapping = {"\t": "\\t", "\r": "\\r", "\n": "\\n", "\0": "\\0", "\\": "\\\\", "'": "\\'", '"': '\\"'}
+    for char in text:
+        code = ord(char)
+        if code >= 0x20 and code != 0x7F:
+            pieces.append(char)
+        elif char in mapping:
+            pieces.append(mapping[char])
+        else:
+            pieces.append(f"\\u{{{code:x}}}")
+    return "".join(pieces)
+
+
+def escape_name(text: str, quote: bool) -> str:
+    escaped = _escape_control(text)
+    needs_quotes = " " in text or "'" in text
+    if quote and needs_quotes:
+        mark = '"' if "'" in text else "'"
+        return mark + escaped + mark
+    return escaped
+
+
+def _normal_display_path(path: str) -> str:
+    return ntpath.normpath(path)
+
+
+def display_base_name(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> str:
+    if opts.absolute == "on":
+        raw = ntpath.abspath(file.path)
+        return escape_name(_normal_display_path(raw), opts.quote)
+    if opts.absolute == "follow":
+        try:
+            raw = os.path.realpath(file.path)
+        except OSError:
+            raw = ntpath.abspath(file.path)
+        return escape_name(_normal_display_path(raw), opts.quote)
+    prefix = ""
+    if not file.parented:
+        parent = ntpath.dirname(_normal_display_path(file.path))
+        if parent:
+            prefix = escape_name(parent, opts.quote) + "\\"
+    return prefix + escape_name(file.name, opts.quote)
+
+
+def _classify(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> str:
+    if opts.classify != "always":
+        return ""
+    if file.is_dir():
+        return "/"
+    if file.is_link():
+        return "@"
+    return ""
+
+
+def _link_target_text(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> Optional[str]:
+    if not file.is_link() or opts.deref:
+        return None
+    try:
+        target_path = os.readlink(file.path)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    if target_path.startswith("\\\\?\\"):
+        target_path = target_path[4:]
+    target_exists = os.path.exists(file.path)
+    if not target_exists:
+        return escape_name(target_path, opts.quote)
+    parent = ntpath.dirname(_normal_display_path(target_path))
+    name = _path_name(target_path)
+    shown = (escape_name(parent, opts.quote) + "\\" if parent else "") + escape_name(name, opts.quote)
+    try:
+        target_info = FileInfo(target_path if ntpath.isabs(target_path) else ntpath.join(ntpath.dirname(file.path), target_path), name)
+        shown += _classify(target_info, opts)

+def _spec(short: Optional[str], long: str, takes: str = "forbidden", choices=None, default=None):
+    return ArgSpec(short, long, takes, tuple(choices) if choices else None, default)

+

+    _spec(None, "icons", "optional", WHEN_CHOICES, "auto"),

+BY_SHORT = {s.short: s for s in SPECS if s.short is not None}

+class OptionError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Occurrence:
+    spec: ArgSpec
+    shown: str
+    value: Optional[str]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Parsed:
+    occurrences: list[Occurrence] = field(default_factory=list)
+    paths: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def count(self, name: str) -> int:
+        return sum(o.spec.long == name for o in self.occurrences)
+
+    def has(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        return self.count(name) > 0
+
+    def last_value(self, *names: str) -> Optional[str]:
+        wanted = set(names)
+        for occurrence in reversed(self.occurrences):
+            if occurrence.spec.long in wanted and occurrence.value is not None:
+                return occurrence.value
+        return None
+
+    def last_flag(self, *names: str) -> Optional[str]:
+        wanted = set(names)
+        for occurrence in reversed(self.occurrences):
+            if occurrence.spec.long in wanted and occurrence.value is None:
+                return occurrence.spec.long
+        return None
+
+
+def _choices_text(choices: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
+    return "choices: " + ", ".join(choices)
+
+
+def _flag_needs_value(shown: str, choices: Optional[tuple[str, ...]]) -> OptionError:
+    suffix = f" ({_choices_text(choices)})" if choices else ""
+    return OptionError(f"Flag {shown} needs a value{suffix}")
+
+
+def parse_argv(argv: list[str]) -> Parsed:
+    parsed = Parsed()
+    parsing = True
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(argv):
+        token = argv[i]
+        i += 1
+        if not parsing:
+            parsed.paths.append(token)
+            continue
+        if token == "--":
+            parsing = False
+            continue
+        if token.startswith("--"):
+            body = token[2:]
+            before = body
+            after = None
+            if "=" in body:
+                b, a = body.split("=", 1)
+                if b and a:
+                    before, after = b, a
+            spec = BY_LONG.get(before)
+            if spec is None:
+                raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument --{before}")
+            shown = f"--{spec.long}"
+            if after is not None:
+                if spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                    raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, after))
+            elif spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, None))
+            elif spec.takes == "necessary":
+                if i >= len(argv):
+                    raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, argv[i]))
+                i += 1
+            else:
+                if i < len(argv) and spec.choices and argv[i] in spec.choices:
+                    value = argv[i]
+                    i += 1
+                else:
+                    value = spec.default
+                parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+            continue
+        if token.startswith("-") and token != "-":
+            body = token[1:]
+            if "=" in body:
+                before, after = body.split("=", 1)
+                if before and after:
+                    for char in before[:-1]:
+                        spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                        if spec is None:
+                            raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                        shown = f"-{char}"
+                        if spec.takes == "necessary":
+                            raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
+                        value = spec.default if spec.takes == "optional" else None
+                        parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    char = before[-1]
+                    spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                    if spec is None:
+                        raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                    shown = f"-{char}"
+                    if spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                        raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, after))
+                    continue
+            j = 0
+            while j < len(body):
+                char = body[j]
+                spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                if spec is None:
+                    raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                shown = f"-{char}"
+                j += 1
+                if spec.takes == "forbidden":
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, None))
+                elif spec.takes == "necessary":
+                    if j < len(body):
+                        value = body[j:]
+                        j = len(body)
+                    elif i < len(argv):
+                        value = argv[i]
+                        i += 1
+                    else:
+                        raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    break
+                else:
+                    if j < len(body):
+                        value = body[j:]
+                        if spec.choices and value not in spec.choices:
+                            raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
+                        j = len(body)
+                    elif i < len(argv) and spec.choices and argv[i] in spec.choices:
+                        value = argv[i]
+                        i += 1
+                    else:
+                        value = spec.default
+                    parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
+                    break
+            continue
+        parsed.paths.append(token)
+    return parsed
+
+
+def _bad_argument(spec_name: str, value: str) -> OptionError:
+    spec = BY_LONG[spec_name]
+    suffix = f" ({_choices_text(spec.choices)})" if spec.takes == "necessary" and spec.choices else ""
+    escaped = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
+    return OptionError(f'Option {spec.label()} has no "{escaped}" setting{suffix}')
+
+
+def _parse_usize(value: str, source: str) -> int:
+    if not value or not value.isascii() or not value.isdigit():
+        raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: invalid digit found in string')
+    result = int(value, 10)
+    if result > (1 << 64) - 1:
+        raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: number too large to fit in target type')
+    return result
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Options:
+    mode: str = "lines"  # lines, grid, details, grid-details
+    tree: bool = False
+    recurse: bool = False
+    as_file: bool = False
+    level: Optional[int] = None
+    dot_mode: int = 0
+    sort: str = "name"
+    reverse: bool = False
+    dirs_first: bool = False
+    dirs_last: bool = False
+    only_dirs: bool = False
+    only_files: bool = False
+    no_symlinks: bool = False
+    show_symlinks: bool = False
+    ignore_patterns: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    across: bool = False
+    width: Optional[int] = None
+    quote: bool = True
+    classify: str = "never"
+    absolute: str = "off"
+    deref: bool = False
+    follow_links: bool = False
+    hyperlink: bool = False
+    header: bool = False
+    permissions: bool = True
+    filesize: bool = True
+    time_fields: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["modified"])
+    time_style: str = "default"
+    size_style: str = "decimal"
+    file_flags: bool = False
+    stdin: bool = False
+
+
+def deduce_options(parsed: Parsed) -> Options:
+    opts = Options()
+
+    width_value = parsed.last_value("width")
+    if width_value is not None:
+        width = _parse_usize(width_value, BY_LONG["width"].label())
+        opts.width = width if width >= 1 else None
+    elif "COLUMNS" in os.environ:
+        value = os.environ["COLUMNS"]
+        if not value.isdigit():
+            raise OptionError(
+                f'Value "{value}" not valid for environment variable COLUMNS: invalid digit found in string'
+            )
+        opts.width = int(value)
+
+    is_tty = opts.width is not None or sys.stdout.isatty()
+    view_flag = parsed.last_flag("long", "oneline", "grid", "tree")
+    if view_flag is None:
+        opts.mode = "grid" if is_tty else "lines"
+    elif view_flag == "long" or (view_flag == "tree" and parsed.has("long")) or (
+        view_flag == "grid" and parsed.has("long")
+    ):
+        grid_tree_flag = parsed.last_flag("grid", "tree")
+        opts.mode = "grid-details" if grid_tree_flag == "grid" else "details"
+    elif view_flag == "tree":
+        opts.mode = "details"
+    elif view_flag == "oneline":
+        opts.mode = "lines"
+    else:
+        opts.mode = "grid"
+
+    requested_tree = parsed.has("tree")
+    opts.tree = requested_tree and opts.mode == "details"
+    opts.recurse = opts.tree or parsed.has("recurse")
+    opts.as_file = (parsed.has("treat-dirs-as-files") or parsed.has("list-dirs")) and not opts.recurse
+
+    level_value = parsed.last_value("level")
+    if level_value is not None:
+        opts.level = _parse_usize(level_value, BY_LONG["level"].label())
+
+    all_count = parsed.count("all")
+    if all_count >= 2 and requested_tree:
+        raise OptionError("Option --tree is useless given --all --all")
+    opts.dot_mode = 2 if all_count >= 2 else (1 if all_count or parsed.has("almost-all") else 0)
+
+    sort_value = parsed.last_value("sort")
+    aliases = {
+        "name": "name", "filename": "name", "Name": "Name", "Filename": "Name",
+        ".name": ".name", ".filename": ".name", ".Name": ".Name", ".Filename": ".Name",
+        "size": "size", "filesize": "size", "ext": "extension", "extension": "extension",
+        "Ext": "Extension", "Extension": "Extension", "date": "modified", "time": "modified",
+        "mod": "modified", "modified": "modified", "new": "modified", "newest": "modified",
+        "age": "age", "old": "age", "oldest": "age", "ch": "changed", "changed": "changed",
+        "acc": "accessed", "accessed": "accessed", "cr": "created", "created": "created",
+        "type": "type", "none": "none",
+    }
+    if sort_value is not None:
+        if sort_value not in aliases:
+            raise _bad_argument("sort", sort_value)
+        opts.sort = aliases[sort_value]
+
+    opts.reverse = parsed.has("reverse")
+    opts.dirs_first = parsed.has("group-directories-first")
+    opts.dirs_last = parsed.has("group-directories-last")
+    opts.only_dirs = parsed.has("only-dirs")
+    opts.only_files = parsed.has("only-files")
+    opts.no_symlinks = parsed.has("no-symlinks")
+    opts.show_symlinks = parsed.has("show-symlinks")
+    ignore = parsed.last_value("ignore-glob")
+    opts.ignore_patterns = [] if ignore is None else ignore.split("|")
+    opts.across = parsed.has("across")
+    opts.quote = not parsed.has("no-quotes")
+    opts.deref = parsed.has("dereference")
+    opts.follow_links = parsed.has("follow-symlinks")
+    opts.hyperlink = parsed.has("hyperlink")
+
+    classify = parsed.last_value("classify")
+    if classify is not None:
+        if classify not in ("always", "auto", "automatic", "never"):
+            raise _bad_argument("classify", classify)
+        opts.classify = "always" if classify == "always" else ("always" if classify in ("auto", "automatic") and sys.stdout.isatty() else "never")
+
+    absolute = parsed.last_value("absolute")
+    if absolute is not None:
+        mapping = {"on": "on", "yes": "on", "follow": "follow", "off": "off", "no": "off"}
+        if absolute not in mapping:
+            raise _bad_argument("absolute", absolute)
+        opts.absolute = mapping[absolute]
+
+    opts.header = parsed.has("header")
+    opts.permissions = not parsed.has("no-permissions")
+    opts.filesize = not parsed.has("no-filesize")
+    opts.file_flags = parsed.has("flags")
+    if parsed.has("bytes") and (not parsed.has("binary") or parsed.last_flag("binary", "bytes") == "bytes"):
+        opts.size_style = "bytes"
+    elif parsed.has("binary"):
+        opts.size_style = "binary"
+
+    time_word = parsed.last_value("time")
+    selected = []
+    if parsed.has("no-time"):
+        selected = []
+    elif time_word is not None:
+        tmapping = {"mod": "modified", "modified": "modified", "ch": "changed", "changed": "changed", "acc": "accessed", "accessed": "accessed", "cr": "created", "created": "created"}
+        if time_word not in tmapping:
+            raise _bad_argument("time", time_word)
+        selected = [tmapping[time_word]]
+    else:
+        for flag_name in ("modified", "changed", "created", "accessed"):
+            if parsed.has(flag_name):
+                selected.append(flag_name)
+        if not selected:
+            selected = ["modified"]
+    opts.time_fields = selected
+
+    time_style = parsed.last_value("time-style")
+    if time_style is None:
+        time_style = os.environ.get("TIME_STYLE") or "default"
+    if time_style not in ("default", "relative", "iso", "long-iso", "full-iso") and not time_style.startswith("+"):
+        raise _bad_argument("time-style", time_style)
+    opts.time_style = time_style
+    opts.stdin = parsed.has("stdin") or not sys.stdin.isatty()
+    return opts
+

+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY = 0x00000001
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN = 0x00000002
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM = 0x00000004
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY = 0x00000010
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE = 0x00000020
+FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT = 0x00000400
+
+
+def _path_name(path: str) -> str:
+    normalized = ntpath.normpath(path)
+    name = ntpath.basename(normalized)
+    if name:
+        return name
+    if path in (".", ".."):
+        return path
+    drive, tail = ntpath.splitdrive(normalized)
+    return tail or drive or path
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FileInfo:
+    path: str
+    name: str
+    parented: bool = False
+    is_all_all: bool = False
+    _lstat: Optional[os.stat_result] = None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def argument(cls, path: str) -> "FileInfo":
+        return cls(path=path, name=_path_name(path))
+
+    @classmethod
+    def child(cls, directory: str, name: str, st: Optional[os.stat_result] = None) -> "FileInfo":
+        return cls(path=ntpath.join(directory, name), name=name, parented=True, _lstat=st)
+
+    def lstat(self) -> os.stat_result:
+        if self._lstat is None:
+            self._lstat = os.lstat(self.path)
+        return self._lstat
+
+    def followed_stat(self) -> os.stat_result:
+        return os.stat(self.path)
+
+    def attrs(self) -> int:
+        st = self.lstat()
+        attrs = getattr(st, "st_file_attributes", 0)
+        if attrs:
+            return int(attrs)
+        result = 0
+        if _stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY
+        elif _stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE
+        if not os.access(self.path, os.W_OK):
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY
+        if self.is_link():
+            result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT
+        return result
+
+    def is_link(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISLNK(self.lstat().st_mode) or bool(self.attrs() & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT and os.path.islink(self.path))
+
+    def is_dir(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISDIR(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()
+
+    def is_file(self) -> bool:
+        return _stat.S_ISREG(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()
+
+    def points_to_dir(self) -> bool:
+        if self.is_dir():
+            return True
+        if self.is_link():
+            try:
+                return os.path.isdir(self.path)
+            except OSError:
+                return False
+        return False
+
+    def length(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.lstat().st_size)
+
+    def extension(self) -> Optional[str]:
+        pos = self.name.rfind(".")
+        return None if pos < 0 else self.name[pos + 1 :].lower()
+
+    def time_ns(self, which: str, deref: bool = False) -> Optional[int]:
+        try:
+            st = self.followed_stat() if deref and self.is_link() else self.lstat()
+        except OSError:
+            return None
+        if which in ("modified", "changed"):
+            return int(st.st_mtime_ns)
+        if which == "accessed":
+            return int(st.st_atime_ns)
+        birth_ns = getattr(st, "st_birthtime_ns", None)
+        return int(birth_ns if birth_ns is not None else st.st_ctime_ns)
+
+
+_NATURAL_PARTS = re.compile(r"(\d+)")
+
+
+def _natural_chunks(value: str, insensitive: bool) -> list[tuple[int, object, object]]:
+    if insensitive:
+        value = value.lower()
+    chunks: list[tuple[int, object, object]] = []
+    for part in _NATURAL_PARTS.split(value):
+        if not part:
+            continue
+        if part.isdigit():
+            significant = part.lstrip("0") or "0"
+            chunks.append((0, len(significant), significant))
+        else:
+            chunks.append((1, part, ""))
+    return chunks
+
+
+def _compare_values(a, b) -> int:
+    return (a > b) - (a < b)
+
+
+def _natural_compare(a: str, b: str, insensitive: bool) -> int:
+    ac = _natural_chunks(a, insensitive)
+    bc = _natural_chunks(b, insensitive)
+    for left, right in zip(ac, bc):
+        result = _compare_values(left, right)
+        if result:
+            return result
+    return _compare_values(len(ac), len(bc))
+
+
+def compare_files(a: FileInfo, b: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> int:
+    field_name = opts.sort
+    if field_name == "none":
+        return 0
+    if field_name in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name"):
+        an = a.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and a.name.startswith(".") else a.name
+        bn = b.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and b.name.startswith(".") else b.name
+        return _natural_compare(an, bn, field_name in ("name", ".name"))
+    if field_name in ("extension", "Extension"):
+        ae, be = a.extension(), b.extension()
+        if ae is None or be is None:
+            result = _compare_values(ae is not None, be is not None)
+        else:
+            result = _compare_values(ae, be)
+        if result:
+            return result
+        return _natural_compare(a.name, b.name, field_name == "extension")
+    if field_name == "size":
+        return _compare_values(a.length(), b.length())
+    if field_name in ("modified", "changed", "accessed", "created", "age"):
+        left = a.time_ns(field_name if field_name != "age" else "modified", opts.deref)
+        right = b.time_ns(field_name if field_name != "age" else "modified", opts.deref)
+        lk = (-1 if left is None else left)
+        rk = (-1 if right is None else right)
+        result = _compare_values(lk, rk)
+        return -result if field_name == "age" else result
+    if field_name == "type":
+        def rank(f: FileInfo) -> int:
+            if f.is_dir(): return 0
+            if f.is_file(): return 1
+            return 7
+        result = _compare_values(rank(a), rank(b))
+        return result or _natural_compare(a.name, b.name, False)
+    return 0
+
+
+def sort_files(files: list[FileInfo], opts: Options) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    files.sort(key=functools.cmp_to_key(lambda a, b: compare_files(a, b, opts)))
+    if opts.reverse:
+        files.reverse()
+    if opts.dirs_first:
+        files.sort(key=lambda f: not f.points_to_dir())
+    elif opts.dirs_last:
+        files.sort(key=lambda f: f.points_to_dir())
+    return files
+
+
+def _ignored(name: str, patterns: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
+    return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern) for pattern in patterns)
+
+
+def filter_children(files: list[FileInfo], opts: Options, is_recurse: bool) -> list[FileInfo]:
+    result = [f for f in files if not _ignored(f.name, opts.ignore_patterns)]
+    filtered: list[FileInfo] = []
+    for f in result:
+        keep = True
+        if opts.only_dirs and not opts.only_files:
+            keep = f.is_dir() or (opts.show_symlinks and f.points_to_dir())
+        elif opts.only_files and not opts.only_dirs:
+            if is_recurse:
+                keep = True
+            elif opts.show_symlinks:
+                keep = f.is_file() or (f.is_link() and not f.points_to_dir())

+            while be < len(b) and "0" <= b[be] <= "9": be += 1
+            arun, brun = a[ai:ae], b[bi:be]
+            asignificant, bsignificant = arun.lstrip("0"), brun.lstrip("0")
+            avalue = asignificant or "0"
+            bvalue = bsignificant or "0"
+            result = _compare_values(len(avalue), len(bvalue)) or _compare_values(avalue, bvalue)
+            if result:
+                return result
+            if avalue != "0" and len(arun) != len(brun):

+            if avalue == "0" and len(arun) != len(brun):
+                return _compare_values(len(arun), len(brun))
+            ai, bi = ae, be
+            continue
+        result = _compare_values(ac, bc)
+        if result:
+            return result
+        ai += 1
+        bi += 1
+    return _compare_values(len(a) - ai, len(b) - bi)

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: eza_port.py
@@
-    level_value = parsed.last_value("level")
-    if level_value is not None:
+    level_value = parsed.last_value("level")
+    if level_value is not None and opts.recurse:
         opts.level = _parse_usize(level_value, BY_LONG["level"].label())
@@
     classify = parsed.last_value("classify")
@@
         opts.classify = "always" if classify == "always" else ("always" if classify in ("auto", "automatic") and sys.stdout.isatty() else "never")
+
+    colour = parsed.last_value("color", "colour")
+    if colour is not None and colour not in ("always", "auto", "automatic", "never"):
+        raise _bad_argument("color", colour)
+    icons = parsed.last_value("icons")
+    if icons is not None and icons not in ("always", "auto", "automatic", "never"):
+        raise _bad_argument("icons", icons)
@@
     except OptionError as error:
         _write_utf8(sys.stderr, f"eza: {error}\n")
         if str(error).startswith('Option --time (-t) has no "r" setting'):
             _write_utf8(sys.stderr, 'To sort oldest files last, try "--sort oldest", or just "-sold"\n')
+        elif str(error).startswith("Flag -t needs a value"):
+            _write_utf8(sys.stderr, 'To sort newest files last, try "--sort newest", or just "-snew"\n')
         return 3
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

@@
 def _normal_display_path(path: str) -> str:
     return ntpath.normpath(path)
 
 
+def _display_parent(path: str) -> str:
+    # Path::parent keeps leading `.` and `..` components and the spelling of
+    # separators, while dropping redundant interior current-directory
+    # components.  It does not clean parent-directory components.
+    raw = path.rstrip("\\/")
+    slash = max(raw.rfind("\\"), raw.rfind("/"))
+    if slash < 0:
+        return ""
+    parent = raw[:slash]
+    while parent.endswith("\\.") or parent.endswith("/."):
+        parent = parent[:-2].rstrip("\\/")
+    return parent
+
+
 def display_base_name(file: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> str:
@@
     prefix = ""
     if not file.parented:
-        parent = ntpath.dirname(_normal_display_path(file.path))
+        parent = _display_parent(file.path)
         if parent:
             prefix = escape_name(parent, opts.quote) + "\\"
@@
-    parent = ntpath.dirname(_normal_display_path(target_path))
+    parent = _display_parent(target_path)
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

const r = await tools.shell_command({command: "@'
import pathlib, subprocess, sys
root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
ref = pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip()
port = [sys.executable, 'eza_port.py']
cases = [
 ['-1', './_probe_fixture/alpha.txt'],
 ['-1', r'.\_probe_fixture\alpha.txt'],
 ['-1', '_probe_fixture/./alpha.txt'],
 ['-1', '_probe_fixture/dirA/../alpha.txt'],
 ['-d', '-1', './_probe_fixture/alpha.txt'],
 ['--tree', '--level=1', './_probe_fixture'],
 ['--tree', '--level=1', r'.\_probe_fixture'],
 ['--tree', '--level=1', '_probe_fixture/./dirA'],
 ['--tree', '--level=1', '_probe_fixture/dirA/..'],
]
failed = 0
for args in cases:
    a = subprocess.run([ref, '--color=never', '--icons=never', *args], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    b = subprocess.run([*port, '--color=never', '--icons=never', *args], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    ok = (a.returncode, a.stdout, a.stderr) == (b.returncode, b.stdout, b.stderr)
    print(('OK  ' if ok else 'FAIL'), repr(args))
    if not ok:
        failed += 1
        print(' ref ', a.returncode, repr(a.stdout), repr(a.stderr))
        print(' port', b.returncode, repr(b.stdout), repr(b.stderr))
print(f'{len(cases)-failed}/{len(cases)} exact')
raise SystemExit(bool(failed))

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:

- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.

You are in a benchmark workspace containing a Rust reference application at ./rust-reference and an official reference CLI path recorded in ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt.

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.
